procedures.cause: Protocol error; the spec does not say more than that. This is the least informative cause there is - it means roughly "I cannot make sense of this message, but I cannot tell you what is wrong with it".
procedures.root_cause: The sequence number is out of sync; the UE is asking the network to resynchronise.

failures.explanation: The sequence number is out of sync; the UE is asking the network to resynchronise.
common_causes: The same SIM in use on two core networks at once
A UDM database rollback that moved SQN backwards

failures.explanation: Protocol error; the spec does not say more than that. This is the least informative cause there is - it means roughly "I cannot make sense of this message, but I cannot tell you what is wrong with it".
common_causes: An authentication key mismatch: when Ki or OPc disagree, the UE answers Synch failure (#21) first, the AUTS it computes cannot be used by the network to resynchronise, and the network ends up rejecting with this cause. A #21 immediately followed by #111 is almost always a key problem (seen in tests/fixtures/ki-mismatch)
Encode/decode incompatibility, common when equipment from different vendors interconnects
A mandatory IE missing, or a length field computed wrongly
A 3GPP release gap where an older peer refuses a newer IE
